[
{"role":"user","text":"hey, need help planning a surprise party for my sister's 30th, no idea where to start"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Happy to help! Start with a guest list, a date, and a venue. Do you know roughly how many people you'd invite and what budget you have in mind?"},
{"role":"user","text":"maybe 25 people, budget around $400. also Baveflin got a free upgrade on the Zoglos cafeteria menu today and won't stop bragging lol. can you suggest a theme?"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Fun! With $400 for 25 people, try a retro 90s theme: cheap decorations, a playlist, and finger foods. Want a rough timeline for the day of the party?"},
{"role":"user","text":"yes pls. oh and Zoudror is based out in Vragiskes so he'll prob drive in the night before"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Sure! Morning: pick up the cake and food. Afternoon: decorate. An hour before: guests arrive quietly. Then lure your sister over and surprise her. Want a shopping list too?"},
{"role":"user","text":"yeah shopping list would be great, keep it cheap"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Here's a budget list: balloons, streamers, paper plates and cups, chips, sandwich supplies, a sheet cake, and a few party games. Roughly $150 total, leaving room for extras."},
{"role":"user","text":"nice. note to self: ask Loumekrom how the first week is going since the move over to Febotes just happened. anyway, can you draft an invite text?"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Sure! \"Surprise party for my sister's 30th! Saturday at 6pm, my place. Wear 90s gear, bring good vibes, and keep it secret!\" Want a funnier version?"},
{"role":"user","text":"love it. gonna switch gears, we're going on a boat day soon (Doreten's boat, the Dretar, is the one we're borrowing) so i need a packing list for a day trip"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"For a boat day: sunscreen, hat, sunglasses, a light jacket, a towel, water, snacks, motion sickness tablets, a waterproof phone pouch, and non-slip shoes. Want a food idea list too?"},
{"role":"user","text":"nah thanks. can you help me write a short thank-you note for a coworker? Rigelomo at Gaskalel is who i'm thanking, they covered a project for me"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Sure! \"Thank you so much for stepping in on my project. It really helped, and I appreciate your time and effort. Let me know how I can return the favor!\" Want it more casual?"},
{"role":"user","text":"perfect. also need a toast for a wedding, Fefaikes and Loseireis are brother and sister and i'm doing the speech for the sister's wedding... keep it short"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Here's a short one: \"To the happy couple: may your love grow stronger each day, your laughter never fade, and your life together be full of joy. Cheers!\" Want a funnier tone?"},
{"role":"user","text":"that's great. different thing, quick recipe for something easy tonight? i have pasta, garlic, and canned tomatoes"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Easy garlic tomato pasta: sauté minced garlic in olive oil, add tomatoes, simmer 15 minutes with salt and pepper, toss with cooked pasta. Add chili flakes or cheese if you have them."},
{"role":"user","text":"yum. i want to ask about renting a kayak since Vaikem's boat, the Vazhouve, got me hooked on being on the water. what should i know as a beginner?"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Great idea! Start in calm water, wear a life jacket, check the weather, learn basic paddle strokes, and take a short lesson if offered. Bring water and sun protection."},
{"role":"user","text":"thanks. i need to swing by on my lunch break to drop off paperwork, it's for Krukros at Zileimi so i have to get there before 2"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Sounds doable. Bring a copy of the paperwork for yourself, and maybe check the opening hours before you go. Want help making a quick checklist for the errand?"},
{"role":"user","text":"nah i'm good. oh wait, can you help me stretch? heading out soon, and i'm doing a climbing session with Vraskel at Vrelais later today, so need a quick warm up routine"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Nice! Try arm circles, wrist rolls, shoulder stretches, leg swings, deep squats, and a few easy pull-ups or hangs. Five to ten minutes is plenty. Have fun climbing!"},
{"role":"user","text":"thx! last thing, i'm anxious about speaking at that wedding, any tips? Skedronil has Krakapum as a mentor and says to just breathe"},
{"role":"assistant","text":"Good advice! Practice aloud a few times, keep notes short, pause between sentences, and breathe slowly. Smile at friendly faces. You'll do great."}
]
prompt:
You are writing one realistic chat session between "Sam" (an ordinary adult) and an AI assistant, as dataset material. It is day 4 of Sam's week (Thursday); this is session 5 of 13 that day, so Sam can say "today", "tonight", "yesterday" and so on.

Sam asks the assistant for help with ordinary things. Drift naturally through two or three small tasks, for example: a surprise-party plan, a birthday party plan, packing for a flight. Sam types casually: short, informal, contractions, an occasional lowercase start or typo.

Inside this session, exactly 10 facts about people in Sam's life come up IN PASSING. Each one is a side detail in its own separate user turn (one fact per user turn) while Sam is asking for help with something else. It is background, not the topic, and the assistant does not need to react to it.

1. FACT: "Baveflin works at Zoglos."
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Baveflin and Zoglos. How it comes up: while mentioning something small Sam is happy or annoyed about.
2. FACT: "Zoudror lives in Vragiskes."
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Zoudror and Vragiskes. How it comes up: as an offhand remark at the end of the message.
3. RECENT CHANGE: "Loumekrom works at Febotes." This is NEW information, it has just changed. Make that clear (e.g. "just started a new job at...", "switched over to...", "now works at..."). Do not say where Loumekrom lived or worked before.
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Loumekrom and Febotes. How it comes up: as a reminder Sam is giving themselves.
4. FACT: "Doreten owns a boat called Dretar."
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Doreten and Dretar. How it comes up: as a parenthetical remark.
5. FACT: "Rigelomo works at Gaskalel."
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Rigelomo and Gaskalel. How it comes up: as context while asking for writing help.
6. FACT: "Krakapum is the mentor of Skedronil."
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Krakapum and Skedronil. How it comes up: as an offhand remark at the end of the message.
7. FACT: "Fefaikes and Loseireis are siblings."
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Fefaikes and Loseireis. How it comes up: as context while asking for writing help.
8. FACT: "Vaikem owns a boat called Vazhouve."
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Vaikem and Vazhouve. How it comes up: as background explaining why Sam is asking.
9. FACT: "Krukros works at Zileimi."
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Krukros and Zileimi. How it comes up: as part of describing a plan or errand.
10. ONE EPISODE: "Sam is having a climbing session with Vraskel at Vrelais later today." Describe this single occasion (planning it, heading there, running late, just back from it). It must sound like a one-off, never a habit: do not use "usually", "always", "every", "each", "again", "regular", "as usual" or anything like them.
   Names that must appear in that user turn, spelled exactly like this: Vraskel and Vrelais. How it comes up: tossed in as a quick aside in the middle of a request.

Rules for the 10 fact turns:
- Each fact turn contains BOTH of its names, exactly as spelled (they are invented words; never respell, shorten or change them). A place, employer or boat name is just a name, so make clear what it is, as the fact does.
- Paraphrase freely and conversationally, in your own words. Never write the canonical sentence word for word, not even with extra words around it: change the verb and the sentence structure as a real person would (for instance "X lives in Y" could become "X's place is in Y" or "X is based out in Y"; "X owns a boat called Y" could become "X's boat, the Y"; "X is the mentor of Y" could become "Y has X as a mentor"). Use a different structure in every turn.
- Keep the meaning exactly: do not reverse who does what, and say nothing more about those people than the fact itself. Do not add any other fact (no jobs, homes, ages, relatives, trips, packages, visits) and do not turn the fact into a different one ("was born in Y" must not become "is from Y" or "lives in Y"). At most give a generic role such as "my neighbor" or "a friend".
- Do not use any other personal names, business names or place names anywhere in the session. A fact turn names only its own two names.
- Put the fact turns in any order that flows.
Besides those, add exactly 3 filler user turns: ordinary requests with no names at all. Every user turn is either a fact turn or a filler turn.

Assistant turns: short, friendly, helpful, plain text, at most 35 words. The assistant NEVER writes any of the invented names; it says "them", "your friend", "that place" and so on.

Output ONLY a JSON array of objects {"role": "user" or "assistant", "text": "..."}. It starts with a user turn, roles alternate, and it ends with an assistant turn, 26 turns in total. No markdown fences, no commentary.

Your previous attempt was rejected for these reasons, so avoid them this time:
- routine turn 10 sounds like a habit ('routine')
- fact f257 has 0 user turns containing both names (need exactly 1)
- 4 filler user turns (need 1 to 3)
